newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end modestly up on CVRD woes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end modestly up on CVRD woes.

text.p: Brazil shares closed slightly higher in moderate trade with major investors on the sidelines on concerns that Tuesday's auction of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) will be delayed, brokers said.
"Worries over the CVRD sale kept most investors out of the bolsa," one senior trader said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded stocks ended up 0.31 percent at 9,762 points. Volume was a moderate 456 million reais ($430.1 million), below recent market daily average of $500-$600 million.

A host of legal challenges has been threatening the scheduled CVRD auction at 1000 local/1300 GMT on April 29. So far, six court injunctions have been filed in four regional courts suspending the auction.
The government said it would appeal against the rulings, but so far it has failed to have any injunction revoked.
Worries over the CVRD sale led the company's preferred shares of Vale do Rio Doce, which are the most liquid, to close off 0.37 percent at 26.90 reais, traders said.
The company's voting stock dropped 1.38 percent, ending at 28.50 reais.

The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, ended up 0.13 percent at 2,672 points, with federal Eletrobras rising 0.87 percent to 503 reais.
Analysts expect the market to be nervous at Tuesday's open as it remains unclear whether or not CVRD will be auctioned off as planned.
